data.name: Pontius
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'pontis', meaning 'bridge'. This name was given to individuals who lived near or managed a bridge in ancient Rome. In Christian history, Pontius Pilate was a Roman prefect who infamously condemned Jesus Christ to death.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes a connection or passage to a higher spiritual understanding.

in_hebrew.name: פונטיוס
in_hebrew.meaning: משמעות של שם פונטיוס: שדה, שטח, שם
in_hebrew.long_meaning: שם פונטיוס בעברית: פונטיוס הוא שם רומי שמקורו בשפה הלטינית, ומשמעותו 'שדה' או 'שטח'. במסורת הנוצרית, פונטיוס היה שם של קומודיאנוס, הסופר לבניו של פלאביאנוס, וגם שם של פלאביוס יוליוס, הקיסר הרומי שהוצא להורג בשנת 96 לספירה. בספרות הנוצרית, פונטיוס הוא שם של קדוש, שהונצרך בספר 'אקטס של השליחים'.

in_greek.name: Πόντιος
in_greek.meaning: σημασία του ονόματος Πόντιος: γη, έδαφος, όνομα
in_greek.long_meaning: όνομα Πόντιος στα ελληνικά: Πόντιος είναι ελληνικό όνομα που προέρχεται από την λατινική γλώσσα, και σημαίνει 'γη' ή 'έδαφος'. Στην αιώνια παράδοση της Εκκλησίας, Πόντιος ήταν όνομα του Κομόδιανου, τού σοφού του Φλάβιου Β΄, και επίσης όνομα του Φλαβίου Ιουλίου, του Ρωμαίου αυτοκράτορα που εκτελέστηκε το έτος 96 μετά Χριστόν. Στην αιώνια παράδοση της Εκκλησίας, Πόντιος είναι όνομα αγίου, ο οποίος αγιοποιήθηκε στο βιβλίο των 'Δραμάτων των Αποστόλων'.

in_latin.name: Pontius
in_latin.meaning: significatio nominis Pontius: campus, terra, nomen
in_latin.long_meaning: nomen Pontius in latino: Pontius est nomen Romanum, quod significat 'campus' aut 'terra'. In historia Ecclesiae, Pontius fuit nomen Commodiani, sapientis Filii Flaviani, et quoque nomen Flavii Iulii, Imperatoris Romanorum qui exsecutus est anno 96 post Christum. In historia Ecclesiae, Pontius est nomen sancti, qui sanctificatus est in libro 'Actuum Apostolorum'.

in_english.name: Pontius
in_english.meaning: meaning of the name Pontius: field, ground, name
in_english.long_meaning: name Pontius in English: Pontius is a Roman name that originates from the Latin language, and means 'field' or 'ground'. In Christian tradition, Pontius was the name of Commodianus, the wise son of Flavian II, and also the name of Flavius Julius, the Roman Emperor who was executed in 96 AD. In Christian tradition, Pontius is a name of a saint, who was canonized in the book 'Acts of the Apostles'.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Pontius' brings to mind the image of a significant figure in Roman history, responsible for managing the infrastructure of civilization. Despite its pagan origin, it has been embraced by the Christian faith due to the most famous bearer of this name – Pontius Pilate.
data.spiritual_significance: Pontius Pilate's name is synonymous with conviction and brutality in the Christian story. He stands as a symbol of human responsibility in the face of moral dilemmas and the extensiveness of God's love towards humanity, even during acts of violence and injustice. The spiritual significance of this name is a reminder to face challenges with courage and conviction while acknowledging the power of redemption and forgiveness.

historical_references.reference: Pontius Pilate was the Roman prefect of Judea from 26 to 31 AD. He is most famous for presiding over the trial of Jesus of Nazareth and ordering his crucifixion.
Pontius Agrippa was a king of the territory of Judea from 41 to 48 AD. He is mentioned in the New Testament as having heard Paul’s defense before Agrippa and being impressed by his arguments.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Pontius is of Roman origin, derived from the Latin word 'pontifex' meaning 'bridge builder'. In modern times, this name has gained significance in various fields, including Roman history, biblical studies, and legal and judicial fields. In Roman history, Pontius Pilate is a well-known figure, having served as the prefect (governor) of Judea from AD 26 to 31. His most infamous act was the trial and sentencing of Jesus of Nazareth. In biblical studies, scholars continue to debate the historical accuracy of the Pontius Pilate account and delve deeper into the political climate of the Roman Empire during his tenure. In the legal and judicial fields, the name Pontius is associated with various legal decisions and court cases. For instance, in the United States, there is a legal precedent named Pontius v. Pontius (1994), which dealt with the interpretation of a contract. Overall, the name Pontius is a fascinating historical name that continues to be relevant in modern times.
